issues.text: decisions/0124 O16 says the bound of 4 000 drawing calls a frame holds for every window up to 3 920 px wide and is exceeded from 3 940 px at scale 2 and 620-639 px high. Measured with the scale rule of tokens.css (4 from 1300 x 700, 3 from 1000 x 640, else 2) and the narrow rule below 760 px, over widths in steps of 2 px: the first window over 4 000 is 3 778 px wide at scale 2 and 639 px high (4 004 calls); 3 920 x 630 draws 4 047; scale 4 reaches 4 007 at 6 760 px and 4 339 at 8 000 px (the O16 maximum). The code is as built and the limit is a named one, so this is no defect of this step: OS-3 asserts at most 4 000 calls up to 3 700 px wide and at most 4 339 above (a room over 2 000 logical px has no stage map: stageMap(2001) is null). For ORCH and the next CODE-DESIGNER edit: the width of O16 is 3 778, not 3 940, if the limit is to be written exactly.

Decisions/0124 H4 and M57: the mutants for ST-5 (the drawScene exception escapes, a null context gets no text-view class) and M57 for ST-4 are run against the unit view here: H4a (no text-view for a null context) red in OV-7; H4b (every catch of makeView rethrows, so the exception leaves view.js) red in OV-7; H4d, H4e, H4f (the class not added, the text list not written, the loop not stopped) red in OV-7; M57 and M57b (a walk with reduced motion; no follow of a change) red in OV-4. The browser tests ST-4 and ST-5 stay T4's. OV-7 is one test with its title extended (the design counts seven OV tests, so no eighth was added).

Equivalent mutants, named so they are not read as missed: M44 'left before right' (0 different, as F25 measured); M56B (no hidden check inside the frame callback: the request that could reach it is cancelled by the visibility handler, and a request is never made while hidden); H4c (drawScene's exception rethrown inside drawFrame: the callers' catch gives the same text view, and nothing leaves the module either way); the camera's `>=` changed to `>` at the end of the time (the eased value at the end rounds to the target); the step frame of a standing walker (stand() resets the walked time, so frame 0 either way); M13b, M13c (a non-object body or answers is refused by the engine with a code that maps to the same bad_body or bad_answers) and M14d (refusalCode returns the reason: only the three reasons that a page can cause reach it); a mutant of the test's own helper that removes OS-4's constant check (the same fault planted in draw.js is red in OS-4 and OS-6, because draw.js's constants are also compared with the test's list); and a reorder of the intake languages (no effect).

What the deep intakes of DM-6 cover and do not: objects nested 20 000 and 30 000 deep and an array nested 50 000 deep overflow the projection before the answer is written, so the questionnaire gives 503 on both ways (SECURITY-REVIEWER L2 of the first pass; verified: with the try of the projection removed the mutant is red). The second-pass L1 of step 03b (an array nested 6 900-9 700 deep that the projection can copy but JSON.stringify cannot write, 500 on the questionnaire) depends on the stack depth of the process at the moment and was not made a test: no depth is stable across runs. It stays open in the review's own words (Low).

A result request whose answers do not reach the broken place of an intake that the loader accepts (an option that is null in a question that is not answered) is 200: the engine reads an option only for an answered question. DM-6 therefore sends an answer to the broken question (the questionnaire reads every option and gives 503 for the same file). This is the engine's behaviour and the design's definition of 'broken' by the loader's rule (step 04b I4).

The floats of the walker: the time walked is summed in floating point, so a frame edge that a test hits exactly (a tick of 0.01 s at 160 ms) can flip one tick late. Not a defect (the original design reads floor(ms / frameMs)); OS-7 and OV tests use steps that never end on an edge so the result does not depend on the sum's last bit.

The scenario of PO-4 that sends a route to a cell that no walker can reach (a closed room of the layout) was added after the first mutant run showed that a list of cells taken from walkable() alone contains cells that no path reaches and the fixtures then never walked; the cells of every other fixture are now taken from the reachable ones and each of the 15 scenarios is asserted to walk in more than 20 ticks.

No test of this sub-step caught an error of the code, and no edit of the code is needed. Known and not mine: `cd tools && npm run handoffs-check` prints the one PENDING line of handoffs/M0DOCS-20261117-01/step-05c-test-designer.json.
